source.snippet: 330 chat messages, 75 finished tasks, and one analyst who announced work she never did. [Title and summary of dev.to post, 12 points, 9 comments, 2026-11-09]

problem_statement: Startup operators deploying multi-agent AI systems find that agents generate high volumes of communication and status announcements without proportional task completion, making it hard to measure real output and trust agent-reported progress.
target_segment: Solo founders and small startup teams (1–5 people) using multi-agent AI frameworks to automate business operations or software development workflows.
notes: Dev.to post (2026-11-09, 12 points, 9 comments) with concrete ratio: 330 messages → 75 real tasks. Signals a monitoring/verification gap for multi-agent systems. Overlaps with the unit-test governance opportunity but from an operator rather than engineering-team angle. Buyer is a founder already spending money on AI agent infrastructure (API costs, orchestration tools). A lightweight agent-output auditing or task-verification layer could be sold as a SaaS add-on. Signal is moderate — single post but engagement suggests resonance.
